subject: Data Engineering
title: Compaction and Optimization
description: A 60-second lesson on Compaction and Optimization.

hook.text: After a week of streaming ingestion, a table has 100,000 tiny files. Queries are 10x slower than they should be.

buildup.text: Compaction merges many small files into fewer large files, reducing metadata overhead and improving read speed.

discovery.text: Table formats provide OPTIMIZE commands that rewrite files into the ideal size — typically 128 MB to 1 GB.

twist.text: Compaction itself is a write-heavy operation. Schedule it during low-traffic windows to avoid resource contention.

climax.text: Regular compaction keeps lakehouse performance high as data accumulates from continuous writes.

punchline.text: Compact the small files. Restore the speed.

quiz.question: What does compaction do in a lakehouse?
options: Merges small files into larger ones for better query performance
